title: The Fundamental Principles of Bioethics
audience: Basic science learners applying bioethical principles to biomedical AI
objectives: Identify the four principles of bioethics in an AI disease-risk prediction case.
Explain conflicts between beneficence, non-maleficence, justice, and autonomy.
Justify which principle should guide deployment when AI model bias may reinforce disparities.
Reflect on bias auditing, transparency, community engagement, and IRB or regulatory guidance.

sections.name: Case Study
sections.purpose: Introduce an AI genetic risk model with biased predictions across racial and ethnic groups.
sections.how_to_use: Read the case and identify who benefits, who may be harmed, and where fairness concerns arise.

sections.name: Bioethical Principles
sections.purpose: Map the case to autonomy, beneficence, non-maleficence, and justice.
sections.how_to_use: Select all relevant principles, then optionally compare with the example.

sections.name: Principle Conflicts
sections.purpose: Explain ethical tensions in the deployment decision.
sections.how_to_use: Describe how helping many patients can conflict with avoiding harm and ensuring justice.

sections.name: Precedence
sections.how_to_use: Choose which principle should take priority and explain why.

sections.name: Reflection
sections.purpose: Connect the case to governance and responsible AI development.
sections.how_to_use: Write additional safeguards such as bias audits, stakeholder communication, transparency, or IRB review.

chatbot_guidance: When asked how to use this notebook, guide the learner through the case, principles, conflicts, precedence, and reflection.
For basic science users, emphasize fairness in training data, bias auditing, transparency, and responsible deployment.
Help learners distinguish beneficence from justice and non-maleficence.
